details: Iranian forces seized two container ships and reportedly fired on a third in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, April 23, 2026. This escalation occurred just hours after US President Donald Trump announced an indefinite extension of a ceasefire with Iran. The US continues its naval blockade on Iranian ports, which Tehran views as a violation of the ceasefire, significantly disrupting global oil trade through the critical waterway and intensifying geopolitical instability.
title: Iran Seizes Ships in Hormuz Amid Blockade, US Ceasefire Extended

details: Bitcoin's price surged past $79,000, reaching an almost two-month high, following President Trump's extension of the US-Iran ceasefire. This development fostered a "risk-on" sentiment in the crypto market, bolstered by significant institutional demand, including recent substantial Bitcoin purchases by MicroStrategy. While the ceasefire temporarily eased immediate geopolitical risk perceptions, the underlying tensions suggest potential for continued market volatility.
title: Bitcoin Surges Towards $79K as US-Iran Ceasefire Eases Geopolitical Risk

details: Recent reports from early April 2026 suggested Iran intended to demand Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies as transit tolls for ships navigating the Strait of Hormuz, purportedly to circumvent financial sanctions. However, Iranian state-linked media on April 23 denied these claims. Concurrently, a Greek maritime risk firm, MARISKS, issued a warning about fraudsters impersonating Iranian authorities and demanding cryptocurrency payments for safe passage through the Strait, advising shipping companies that these demands are scams.
title: Iran Denies Crypto Tolls for Hormuz, Scam Alert Raised
